audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives Singed levels 2, 3 and first item, but the whys under those exact rows say Kennen 'can now reliably threaten the stun', 'the lane is his', and that the first-item window is 'where dying to one misstep is most likely'. Levels 4-5 and level 6 are marked Skill while their whys say the proxy window is your power spike and that Slicing Maelstrom 'changes the risk calculus entirely'.
audit.why: Kennen is a 950-range poke mage with a three-stack stun against a melee champion with a 20-unit damage aura and a 125-range Fling. He owns every stage where he can stand still and throw shuriken; Singed owns the stages where the wave is somewhere Kennen cannot reach. 52.13% is Singed edging it on macro, not on lane stages.
audit.corrected: Skill / Kennen / Kennen / Singed / Kennen / Kennen / Singed — which is also the packet chart, and matches every why already written.

audit.whatIsWrong: mid says to commit 'only if his R is provably on cooldown' without ever giving the number, and the packet lists no cooldown-sequencing anywhere near the ult.
audit.why: Slicing Maelstrom is a flat 120s at every rank. That is a very long, very countable window, and it is the single number this lane is played around — the difference between a Singed who commits into a stun-lock and one who walks in free.
audit.corrected: Slicing Maelstrom 120s flat; Thundering Shuriken 7/6.25/5.5/4.75/4; Lightning Rush 10/9/8/7/6; Electrical Surge 13/11.25/9.5/7.75/6.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two kit claims are wrong. (a) whys[2] and wants.foe[1] both say Kennen dashes through Mega Adhesive to deny the root. Lightning Rush is not a dash. (b) whys[1] calls Electrical Surge an auto-reset.
audit.why: Riot Lightning Rush: 'Kennen morphs into a lightning form, enabling him to pass through units and apply a Mark of the Storm. Kennen gains Move Speed when entering this form, and attack speed when leaving it.' Pass-through-units and move speed, no blink and no dash flag in the kit — so he still has to physically cross the puddle and the adhesive slow still applies. Riot Electrical Surge: 'passively deals extra damage and adds a Mark of the Storm to his target every few attacks' — kit flags onHit and zone, no autoReset. Which matters for itemisation: his damage scales with attack speed and is magic, so MR, not armour, reads the trade.
audit.corrected: Lightning Rush is a speed form that crosses Mega Adhesive quickly, not one that skips it; Electrical Surge is on-hit and the reason you build MR.

edits.before: Kennen gains Electrical Surge (W) at level 2 letting him auto-reset for a second Mark of the Storm proc — he can now reliably threaten the stun before your combo is assembled.
edits.after: Electrical Surge is on-hit, not an auto-reset — it marks off his attack speed, so a shuriken plus two autos stuns you at level 2 before your combo exists. Build MR, never armour.

edits.before: Full Thundering Shuriken plus Electrical Surge plus Lightning Rush kit means Kennen can poke, dash through your Mega Adhesive to avoid the root, and still escape Fling range — the lane is his.
edits.after: Lightning Rush is a movement form, not a dash — he still has to cross Mega Adhesive rather than skip it. But 950-range Thundering Shuriken outranges every tool you own, so the lane is his.

edits.before: Use Lightning Rush to pass through your Mega Adhesive zone rather than leaving it, denying your root
edits.after: Use Lightning Rush's move speed to cross Mega Adhesive fast — a form, not a blink, so it cannot skip it

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are your strongest window in this lane — not because you beat Kennen in a trade, but because he cannot stop your proxy. Send yourself behind his tower to farm the mid-wave: he has to walk into your Poison Trail if he chases, and if he ignores you he bleeds gold and plate gold. At level 6 Insanity Potion makes you mobile enough to threaten the all-in, but Kennen's Slicing Maelstrom shuts that down cleanly — only go for the full commit if his R is provably on cooldown and you have Ghost available. The correct mid-game pattern is deny and accelerate, not duel.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your strongest window in this lane — not because you beat Kennen in a trade, but because he cannot stop your proxy. Send yourself behind his tower to farm the mid-wave: he has to walk into your Poison Trail if he chases, and if he ignores you he bleeds gold and plate gold. At 6 Insanity Potion makes you mobile enough to threaten the all-in, but Slicing Maelstrom shuts it down — and it is a flat 120s at every rank, so start the clock the moment it fires and commit inside that gap with Ghost up. Deny and accelerate, never duel.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Kennen must walk into your range.
edits.after: Full kit online, but 950-range shuriken means he never has to walk in. Count his marks and leave at two, every time.

edits.before: - Kennen Lightning Rush: matchup-defining — His escape. Kite when it’s down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Kennen Slicing Maelstrom: flat 120s, and the lane is decided inside that gap — commit only there. - Lightning Rush 10-6s is a speed form, not a blink: it crosses your goo, never skips it. - Insanity Potion 100s: kill windows.

notes: The full layer nominates Lightning Rush as the matchup-defining ability (focus.text, loading, dosFull[0], report[5]). On the kit it is a 10-6s movement form; the ability that actually decides the lane is the 120s Slicing Maelstrom. I corrected breakdown.cooldowns but left focus/loading/dosFull/report[5] pointing at Lightning Rush rather than half-migrating the page — a coherent swap of the focus ability across all five fields is worth doing as one deliberate change.
